ache.title: Auto-battle: the game plays itself, you keep paying
ache.note: Nero reviews Girls’ Frontline 2 Exilium by Sunborn: a detailed interface, character design, story and its gacha. He likes the auto-battle for quick sessions. Auto-battle sounds like respect for your time, but it can turn a game into a check-in you do out of habit. Ask whether you’re playing or just collecting.
watch: gacha slipped into a strategy game
ache.tip: If the game mostly plays itself, ask what you’re getting from it. It’s fine to just stop.
lines: auto-battle: who’s playing, you or it?

videoData.title: Girls' Frontline 2 Exilium: First Impressions & Gameplay Review!

textData.text: In this episode, I dive into Girls' Frontline 2 Exilium, a strategy-oriented game by Sunborn. I share my thoughts on the game's interface, character design, story, and gacha mechanics. The detailed, customizable interface and character models stand out, though the storyline and fanservice might not be for everyone. I also discuss the game's ease of play and auto-battle features, making it accessible for both quick sessions and more extended play. If you're curious about the latest gacha games, this review covers all you need to know!
